## Problem
The `money-market-fund-reflect-yield-positions` Temporal schedule runs `0 0 1-10 * *` (midnight PT, days 1–10). Yield that lands outside that window isn't reflected until the next month's window.

## Change
`lib/temporal/schedules/registry.rb`: `cron_expressions: ['0 0 1-10 * *']` + `time_zone_name: 'America/Los_Angeles'` → `cron_expressions: ['0 * * * *']`. The tz is dropped because hourly-at-:00 fires at the same instants in LA and UTC (whole-hour offset), matching the other `0 * * * *` entries in the registry (none set a tz). Nothing else — not the workflow/activity, `YieldService`, or `frec_yield_event_id`.

(#8685 moved this job from the `cdk8s/schedule.ts` cron + rake task onto the Temporal scheduler; there is no cdk8s entry to change.)

## Scale
10 runs/month → ~720 (72×). Each run makes one `GET /account/{id}/yields` per `AccountProvider::MoneyMarketFund.provisioned` row, via the provider adapter (`app/services/money_market_fund_accounts/yield_service.rb:25-27` → `MoneyMarketFund::Adapters::Frec#fetch_yield_events` → `Frec::Client.yield_events`).

- **Accounts per run (prod console):** `AccountProvider::MoneyMarketFund.where.not(provider_account_id: nil).count` (= `.provisioned`, `money_market_fund.rb:50`) = **46** (49 total). → **46 calls/run ≈ 1,100/day.** The scope has no active/closed filter, so closed MMF accounts are polled too.
- **Baseline Frec traffic** (Datadog APM, `service:net/http @peer.hostname:api.frec.com`, 30d): ~12k calls ≈ 400/day, mostly `/account/{id}` polls. Status mix: 200 ×11,992 · 401 ×46 (one cluster, one week) · 502 ×3 · 400 ×2 · **no 429s**. Total Frec traffic goes to ≈1,500/day, ≈3.75× today's. Retained spans are sampled; treat as floors. Frec's OpenAPI spec (`api.frec.com/api/v1/spec.json`) documents only 200/401 and no rate limit, so headroom is unverified — a same-order burst already exists (the 8h balance check polls every *active* provisioned MMF account, `balance_checks/check_service.rb:272-278`); this raises it from ~3 to ~27 bursts/day. `:00` also coincides with the `*/15` application-refresh and `*/30` pending-orders polls (both per-pending-item, small); kept at `0 * * * *` to match siblings — a minute offset is a one-character change if Frec ever throttles. Note a 429 is rescued per account (`yield_service.rb:80`) and the loop keeps firing the remaining calls back-to-back; an offset alone wouldn't add backoff.
- **On Frec errors:** `Frec::Client.invoke_api` raises on any non-2xx (`lib/frec/client.rb:174`), no retry, no explicit timeout (Net::HTTP 60s defaults). `YieldService` collects per-account errors and raises once at the end (`yield_service.rb:80-84`); other accounts in the same run still get processed.

## Why re-running is a no-op
`money_market_fund_yields` has a **unique index on `(customer_account_id, accrued_on, amount_cents)`** — `idx_mmf_yields_on_account_accrued_amount` (`db/schema.rb:1684`). A yield is identified by account + accrued timestamp + amount and the DB enforces it; `YieldService` rescues `RecordNotUnique` (`yield_service.rb:71-78`) and `receipt_exists?` short-circuits before the insert (`yield_service.rb:97-107`). That constraint, not the frec id, is the real guard — 50/50 yield rows in prod have `frec_yield_event_id = NULL` (prod console) because Frec's `Yield` schema is `{appliedAt, yield}` with no id, so the amount+date path is the only one Frec's contract permits. Corollary: a Frec-side amount revision for the same `appliedAt` would post as a second yield; hourly sampling raises the odds of catching an intermediate value that a midnight poll would miss (hypothetical; Frec documents no revisions).

## Why the old schedule existed
#3540 (Dec 2023): *"Yield accrues on the first weekday of every month. I've just set it to run daily on the first 10 days of each month (accounts for variability in date)."* Prod data: 48/50 yields accrued on days 2–4, so the premise mostly held — but 2 accrued on days 11 and 17, outside the window, where the schedule alone leaves them unreflected until the next month's day 1 (2–3 weeks). Hourly cuts schedule-induced lag from ≤24h in-window / 2–3 weeks out-of-window to ≤1h. (Yields `yield_events` no longer returns for lapsed-contract windows — `reconcile_mmf_balance_check_divergences_task.rb:22-23` — are a separate problem this doesn't touch.)

## Ops notes
- **Rollout:** `Registry.call!` upserts schedules on worker boot (`registry.rb`, `upsert!` → `schedule_handle.update`, preserving pause state), so the new cron applies on deploy with no manual step. `call!` rescues and reports registration failures to Sentry only (`registry.rb:755-756`), so glance at the schedule in the Temporal UI after deploy.
- **Policy:** defaults (`temporalio` `Schedule::Policy#initialize`): `overlap: SKIP` (an overrunning tick is skipped, not stacked), `pause_on_failure: false` (a failed tick doesn't pause the schedule), `catchup_window: 365d` (ticks missed during a Temporal outage are replayed, collapsed by SKIP). `yield_events` takes no date range, so the next tick catches up.
- **Run budget:** the workflow runs the activity with `start_to_close_timeout: 300`, `max_attempts: 1` (`reflect_yield_positions_workflow.rb:9-13`), ≈6.5s per account. Normal runs are seconds — the one retained prod workflow span (APM, 30d) is 9.9s for the full 46-account pass, ~0.2s/call. A hung Frec (60s Net::HTTP defaults) times the activity out server-side after ~5 accounts; the activity doesn't heartbeat so it isn't cancelled (`temporalio` `activity/context.rb:60`) and keeps polling as a zombie. Each request pays TCP connect, TLS, and read under separate 60s Net::HTTP defaults (fresh `Faraday.new` per call), so a stalled Frec costs 60–180s per account (an envelope, not a ceiling — `read_timeout` is per read) → a 46-account pass of ~46 min to ~2.3 h, overlapping the next tick(s) under defaults; a sustained stall spawns a new zombie each tick, so steady state is up to ~3 concurrent zombies ≈ 25% of the schedules fleet's floor capacity (2 pods × 6 slots) (SKIP doesn't apply; the timed-out workflow is already terminal). Ledger stays consistent (per-yield transaction + unique index); cost is a duplicate Frec pass plus, per zombie, one of the schedules fleet's 6 per-pod activity slots and its DB connection held for the zombie's lifetime (`cdk8s/prod-us-west-2-zeus.yaml:43-51`, `connection_management.rb:17-19`). Same mechanism for a merely slow Frec (>6.5s/call): the loop still completes past the deadline and posts everything, but the tick is marked failed. Pre-existing; follow-up is a Faraday timeout on `Frec::Client.connection`.
- **Failure signal:** an activity exception on the final attempt → Sentry via `TemporalUtils::Interceptors::ErrorLogger` (`lib/temporal_utils/interceptors/error_logger.rb:21-22`, `max_attempts: 1` so every raised failure reports). The 300s timeout itself emits nothing; the zombie's eventual exception (if any — e.g. `Faraday::TimeoutError` → `yield_service.rb:84`) reaches Sentry late, tagged to an already-failed run, and a slow-but-succeeding Frec (>6.5s/call, all 2xx) fails the tick with **no Sentry event at all** — only metrics move, and no monitor fires. Datadog: `treasury.temporal.schedules.last_run_status{schedule:money-market-fund-reflect-yield-positions}` flips to 0 on a failed run (`app/jobs/report_temporal_metrics_job.rb:106-112`) — no monitor is defined on it in `ops/datadog/` today, so Sentry is the only alert. A persistent per-account failure therefore surfaces **hourly** until fixed, vs ≤1/day for ≤10 days before — and since the per-provider `rescue` (`yield_service.rb:80`) aborts that account's remaining yields, they stay unposted until the cause is fixed (same as today, just visible sooner), and the gauge pins at 0, masking any other failure. Some noise is expected, not hypothetical: at the observed 502 rate (3/12k) the ~33k yield calls/month imply ~8 transient failures/month ≈ 2 Sentry events/week, each caught up by the next tick. Accepted; a bounded retry around `yield_events` is the follow-up if that's too loud.
